where: Lead and Section 2 (intro plus the Nylon 6 bullet)
problem: The lead says condensation polymers 'come from two bifunctional monomers and lose a small molecule such as water at every link', and Section 2 repeats 'between two monomers ... Every new bond releases one small molecule'. Nylon 6, listed three lines later as a condensation polymer, breaks both statements: it forms from one monomer (caprolactam) by ring opening and loses no small molecule at all, so its repeat-unit mass is identical to the monomer mass. A student who applies the stated rule to nylon 6 will subtract 18 g/mol and get a wrong repeat-unit mass.
fix: Soften the rule and state the exception: 'Condensation polymers are usually made from two bifunctional monomers, with one small molecule such as water or HCl lost per new bond. Nylon 6 is the exception: caprolactam rings open and join head to tail, nothing is lost, and the repeat unit –NH–(CH₂)₅–CO– has the same formula and mass as caprolactam, 113 g/mol.' Subtract water only where it is actually eliminated (nylon 6,6, PET).

problem: 'SBR and nitrile rubber dominate elastomer sales' is not correct. SBR is the largest-volume synthetic rubber, but nitrile rubber is a low-volume specialty rubber used for oil resistance; general-purpose rubbers such as butadiene rubber and natural rubber far outsell it.
fix: 'SBR is the largest-volume synthetic rubber, with butadiene rubber and natural rubber close behind; nitrile rubber is a specialty grade made in much smaller amounts for oil-resistant parts.'

problem: Every other bullet gives the number of small molecules lost per repeat unit, but polycarbonate says only 'HCl leaves'. Since two new carbonate links form per repeat unit, two HCl molecules leave, and a student needs that count for a mass calculation.
fix: 'Polycarbonate: bisphenol A plus phosgene; two HCl molecules leave per repeat unit. Used in helmets and large water jars.'

problem: 'Two entries deserve a second look' introduces a discussion of PTFE, PP and high-density PE — three entries, not two.
fix: 'Three entries deserve a second look.' (or keep 'Two' and drop one of the three discussed).
